source.note: Pain: 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours; arthritis: 400, 600 or 800 mg three or four times daily (every 8 or 6 h). Do not exceed 3200 mg/day, so 800 mg every 4 h would exceed the label.

source.citation: MOTRIN IB (ibuprofen tablets) Product Monograph, McNeil Consumer Healthcare, Health Canada, revised August 9, 2003, p. 2
source.note: 'Oral absorption is estimated to be 80% of the dose.' The US tablet label only says absorption is rapid, with no number. Strictly this is the fraction absorbed, used here as bioavailability.
'The serum half-life is 1.8 to 2.0 hours.' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)
The tablet label gives no Vd; this is the Sun Pharma ibuprofen oral suspension label: 'adults have a volume of approximately 0.12 L/kg'.
'Peak serum ibuprofen levels are generally attained one to two hours after administration.' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)
'45% to 79% of the dose was recovered in the urine within 24 hours'; fraction 0.62 is the midpoint. Free (unchanged) ibuprofen was 'approximately 1%'.

journey.text: Absorbed quickly after swallowing. Blood levels peak within 1 to 2 hours.
Thought to work by blocking prostaglandins, chemicals the body makes that cause pain, fever and swelling.
Quickly broken down and removed in urine. It is almost completely gone within 24 hours of the last dose.
